---
title: "Standardized-evidence flags in a league"
subtitle: "3.4 · a simulated league after the postrank theory book, ch. 17"
description: "Pairwise directions and posterior risk of a thirty-unit flag report."
---

The flag rule groups thirty units according to how far each estimate lies from the league mean in standard error
units. It treats the reference as fixed even though the mean is itself estimated. A unit can receive a higher
flag than a unit with a larger estimate if the two estimates have different precision. The matrix shows the
directions implied by the flags. Once the groups are assigned, we use the posterior to count expected errors
and evaluate reporting risk.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **League, cutoff 1.96.** The flag groups contain 6, 22 and 2 units. They state 188 of 435 pairs. Under the
  teaching posterior, E/N is .130 and risk is .1696. The gray row bands identify units placed below another unit
  whose estimate is smaller; the outlined matrix cells locate the same reversals.
- **Same flags, flat prior.** The report still states 188 pairs. We evaluate the same directions under independent normal posteriors centered on the estimates, with SDs equal to their SEs.
- **League, cutoff 2.576.** The stricter cutoff changes membership of the outer flag groups. The matrix changes in whole blocks:
  all pairs between different flag groups are stated, and all pairs within a group are withheld. A cell within a group leaves the two units unranked.
- **Same report, τ .10.** The same 188 pairs are stated. The all-withheld comparison has risk τ = .10. The cheaper baseline depends on the withholding cost even when the report does not change.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
At the first setting, 20 stated directions reverse the order of the estimates. The largest error probability is
.649 even though the average error probability is below the withholding cost. That difference matters because
the flag rule uses only the estimates and their SEs, with no constraint on the expected errors of individual
comparisons. Both matrix axes follow decreasing estimates. Use the arrow keys or the table to read the cell values.
:::

Standalone: [flags-in-the-league](../../embed/flags-in-the-league.html), for example `?crit=1.96&prior=teaching&tau=.10`.

Related applications: [Grades based on standardized evidence](evidence-flags.qmd), [Posterior summaries in a grade report](../grades/report-card.qmd).
